title: d-12: beads-cache-and-release
description:
## Deliverables
1. Migrate actual beads-cache@8e883ee CacheScheduleStore and scheduler calls to published sc-storage/sc-runtime-db-sqlite/sc-cron0.3.0. Deliver the upstream migration PR and validate app+cron writes through its shared writer, preserving existing data and cron behavior — REQ-RUN-0002; REQ-CRON-0004; ADR-RUN-0020.
2. Own registry runner/workflow, archive rehearsal and actual eight-crate coordinated0.3.0 publication in dependency order with sc-storage first. Run fresh registry-only upstream/cron, server/rmcp and test-util helper consumers with the release-tested dependency combination, with advisory/source/native-identity checks — REQ-RUN-0002/0702; NFR-RUN-0007; ANC-012.
3. Update root README, release notes/project status and applicable controlled-host benchmark evidence to the actual published surface. Preserve kit/recovery rules and do not claim a source checkout or copied facade is the upstream migration — REQ-RUN-0702; NFR-RT-0001.

4. Remove tests/integration/cron-consumer/schema/Cargo.toml rmcp =3.8.0 pin in this sole-owned consumer manifest: use >=3.9 because3.9.x is the tested patched minimum for RUSTSEC-2026-0462 under the ADR-RUN-0203 amendment. Raising the floor removes older vulnerable releases; every later release from3.9 is admitted with no upper bound. Preserve the existing server/default-features selection and run the normal registry consumer tests and apply req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps (ADR-RUN-0203; ANC-037). Also convert tests/integration/cron-consumer/Cargo.toml Windows dev-dependencies to win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0, preserving purpose comments and running the normal Windows tests. d-3/d-5/d-9 retain their own pin-line edits; this sprint does not repeat them.

5. Reuse d-11's check_dependency_manifests(paths) on exact unpacked archives and generated-template defaults; wire it into archive rehearsal, registry consumer validation and upload. Own only input assembly and release fixtures. SDK registry requirements use >= floors with no upper bound; consumer pins are allowed (ANC-037). Remove the interim rule after equivalent sc-lint#936 release and adoption, as recorded by ADR-RUN-0005.

6. After final0.3.0 conversion and registry availability, refresh template/.sc-runtime/** with each supported profile's newest tested registry combination. Use d-11 generation code unchanged to deliver recommended Cargo.lock and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038). Verify metadata/lock agreement and real --locked builds/tests.

## This sprint does not close
Generated app composition/transports are d-11-owned. This sprint starts after d-11 sanity closes and consumes its one manifest checker. No duplicate template wiring, template-only registry subject or second checker.
design:
## Exact released-consumer subject
beads-cache source8e883ee99cb9c34dfb89fb39e25323d54ae6f2ad uses path sc-cron and already stores schedules in its app DB through CacheScheduleStore (`crates/bd-cache-store/src/schedule.rs:80,164`). Record the source and intentional API changes in tests/registry/phase-d/beads-cache/README.md. Migrate that adapter and actual scheduler calls to sc-cron CronStore over Storage<CronRow> backed by the published generic sc-runtime-db-sqlite shared channel writer. Retain existing application/schedule rows, stable identifiers, generation fencing, row limits and atomic multi-row transitions. No local path/patch/Git SDK dependency can satisfy final acceptance. A recorded source reduction is not falsely described as an upstream beads-cache PR having landed; if the actual migration needs an upstream PR, coordinate it with its owner and retain the outcome as a release predicate.
The release-test lock selects the adopted exact release identities for sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-cron and applicable runtime/command packages from crates.io. The exact selection is a release-test identity, not a restrictive production third-party range. Direct rusqlite uses the owner-directed >=0.41 requirement with no upper bound and required bundled/hooks/functions/trace features; d-12 releases that d-6-qualified uncapped range, without a capped qualification fallback. Verify one libsqlite3-sys>=0.39; run normal tests with the selected versions. No SQLx SQLite driver remains in the generated SQLite consumer. SQLx PostgreSQL/MySQL-only graphs must not gain a SQLite native edge; a selected SQLite feature would change that exposure and is not inferred absent from a crate name.

## Registry runner/workflow interface
Own `.github/workflows/phase-d-registry.yml` and `tests/registry/phase-d/run.py` together. The workflow invokes `python3 tests/registry/phase-d/run.py --version <adopted-version> --source crates-io`; the version has one adopted source. It checks the migrated beads-cache subject, server/rmcp and test-util helper subjects, plus the actual migrated beads-cache SQLite+cron application. Isolate registry consumer locks, assert sources/versions using Cargo metadata, execute actual builds/tests and `cargo deny check advisories` without ignoring RUSTSEC-2026-0459/0462. The positive result requires all assertions/audits/tests; missing release/consumer, wrong source/native identity or failed command exits nonzero. Controlled failure inputs prove fail-closed paths; only the actual post-publication run is registry proof. Ordinary inherited source CI is insufficient.
Consumer: release reviewer/maintainers; capability: eight-package published channel writer + shared app storage; observed defect: consumers blocked by native-link/advisory constraints and separate cron topology; delete the dedicated workflow when the standard kit post-publish hook performs the same consumer checks.

## Rehearsal and failure handling
Use the configured kit to package all8 crates. Inspect actual Cargo.toml.orig/normalized manifest, README, features and source comments explaining each extra cap. Unpack exactly these .crate archives into a temporary rehearsal workspace with rehearsal-only patches to their extracted contents; build/test the same consumers before upload. Record hashes; upload those exact archives. This is archive rehearsal, not registry proof. Discard every patch/source replacement and start final proof from fresh registry resolution after publication.
Publish sc-storage first; derive the remaining topological order from final manifests. Existing sc-config/sc-transport and sc-command precede their actual consumers; writer and cron follow sc-storage; sc-runtime and sc-cron-commands follow their applicable prerequisites. All8 adopted versions must be present. Do not invent a fixed order that contradicts actual dependencies.
On mid-sequence transport/index failure, stop, query exact published versions/hashes and retry only missing uploads of identical approved archives. Never republish an occupied version. For a real package/consumer/security defect, stop remaining uploads; release owner yanks newly published defective packages/dependent siblings if leaving them selectable would break consumers or retain a target advisory. Do not yank for transient network/CI errors or unrelated audit findings. An occupied defective version requires source-owner fixes plus a coordinated replacement patch of the adopted train, repeated rehearsal and fresh registry proof; issues remain open on partial/failed publication.

## Required validation and limits
Run `just lint`, `just test`, workspace build, actual `sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml`, normal root/separate-consumer tests (generated proof belongs to d-11) and selected Windows/Monty tests. Install all prerequisites; a documented command is not a pass. Use `python3 scripts/benchmark/check_release_evidence.py`; the newest applicable `site/reports/benchmark-monty/*.campaign.json` + HTML twin must match the source-equivalence contract, otherwise refresh on the existing controlled host procedure. No timing/sleep-based correctness tests. Generated daemon/CLI/schema/wizard wiring is owned by d-11; this dependent sprint proves the upstream application. No synchronization/code generator/config-reload/unspecified permissions work.

Release version is approved coordinated0.3.0 for all8 crates; per-crate rationale is authoritative in run-phase-d design. No0.2.x ScheduleStore removal.


## Independent integration artifacts
Consumes d-3 qualified dependency/API and normal tests, d-4 CLI/action used by publishing-kit tooling, d-5 manifests/contracts/eight-package targets, d-6 generic writer/atomic backend; d-9 CronStore/row migration and d-9 awaited scheduler/command adapter. It consumes d-10 public sc-command combinators and the d-11 manifest-check callable; it does not duplicate d-11 generated daemon wiring or d-7/8 stores. Its registry subjects are actual upstream beads-cache/cron-consumer, server/rmcp and helper. d-12 follows d-11 as the fourth graph wave, consuming its actual checker before final release validation.
Actual beads-cache app and schedule mutations share one writer/file; it has no SQLx SQLite driver, no ATM/sc-compose production dependency and no caller blocking or spawn_blocking. Only dedicated writer runtime uses block_on; reader threads use blocking_recv and no runtime. Dependency declarations follow req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps. Exact SDK0.3.0 release identities are evidence subjects, not third-party production restrictions.
## Internal release order and exact external closure
After d-11 sanity closes, exercise runner fault cases and migrate beads-cache before publication. Before consuming the callable for archive/consumer validation, bd show run-d-11.group-sanity --json must show status=closed with the checker handoff and actual generated integration validation; upload also waits for package-caps to pass on the exact archives. This is a hard sprint prerequisite in the phase index and live dev blocker; the pre-upload check is additional. Also require randlee ratification for pending ADR/template extension and the actual passing safety checks required by the owner sprints; absence keeps publication open, never fake a pass.
After the gate: regenerate canonical Cargo.lock and apply coordinated0.3.0 version bump plus sibling version-to-workspace inheritance in root and owned public manifests/template workspace inputs. In the one exact post-conversion archive rehearsal, validate the actual beads-cache migration against the unpacked archives before the first upload, then publish those exact archives. Discard archive rehearsal patches and run fresh registry-only consumer proofs after upload. Source fixtures are not published proof.
External work owner: beads-cache maintainer (user/randlee), with sprint developer preparing the migration PR. Sprint closure requires upstream PR OPEN and CI GREEN at a recorded SHA against published0.3.0 SDK crates; record URL/SHA and actual source assertions in tests/registry/phase-d/beads-cache/README.md. Merge is not required for sprint/phase closure. If maintainer does not respond, keep d-12/open external follow-up; a fork/draft/source copy is not success. No unauthorized upstream merge. Existing downstream app tests establish its preserved behavior; do not duplicate d-11 generated-app criteria here.
Single canonical root Cargo.lock owner is d-12. Earlier source owners regenerate disposable worktree locks to satisfy each closure tests; they do not commit lock updates. D-12 normalizes one final lock after d-3/d-5/d-6/d-9/d-10 close. Selected native-library proof is cargo tree, never lockfile entries. d-12 takes shared manifest version registration after those named dependency handoffs, leaving0.2.0 development baseline unpublishable until final conversion. Package sc-command exports/README must match d-10 actual helpers.
Root-manifest counterpart: d-12 edits only sc-* release version lines after the d-6 handoff; it never edits the workspace rusqlite line, whose qualified shared range is d-6-owned.
Single-checker ownership: d-11 owns tests/unit/generation/test_runtime_ecosystem_upgrade.py and check_dependency_manifests(paths). d-12 imports it from the integration source, supplies unpacked package/owned test paths through tests/registry/phase-d/run.py and owns test_manifest_gate.py plus its fixture manifests. It never edits or copies the d-11 implementation. The phase index and live blocker edge require d-11 sanity before d-12 dev is ready; source validation uses that delivered artifact. ADR-RUN-0005 interim status/removal are authored by d-5; sc-lint#936 already exists.
acceptance_criteria:
req:REQ-RUN-0002/published-consumers — Actual beads-cache migration PR/revision passes against crates.io0.3.0 packages, no path/patch/Git SDK source. App and schedule writes share its channel writer/file; run the upstream migration subject against published artifacts, distinct from d-11 generated-app criteria. Registry server/rmcp/helper subjects compile and execute; one native libsqlite3-sys identity in the graph, at >=0.39, no SQLx SQLite driver, target SQLite/rmcp advisories clear.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/release — Rehearse exact8crate archives before publication; package manifests/READMEs/features/comments match actual APIs and approved0.3.0. Publish sc-storage first then actual DAG order; all8 versions present, hash-identical retries only for missing uploads. Real defects halt/yank under owner policy and require coordinated replacement patch; transient failures never trigger yanks. Partial upload is not phase success.
req:REQ-RUN-0702/registry-proof — Workflow invokes python3 tests/registry/phase-d/run.py --version 0.3.0 --source crates-io with an isolated release-test lock, source/version assertions and actual upstream tests. Wrong or missing release/source, advisory/native mismatch or failed command exits nonzero. Controlled negatives test refusal; only actual post-publication consumer builds/tests prove delivery. Apply package-caps to the exact unpacked SDK manifests, not consumer-owned pins.
Required commands: just lint; just test; cargo build --workspace; sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml; kit package/rehearsal and fresh registry runner the registry consumers; cargo deny check advisories for every registry subject; python3 scripts/benchmark/check_release_evidence.py with controlled-host evidence matching source-equivalence policy. Root README/release notes match package contents. d-11 generated integration is separately required for phase acceptance.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/publication-gate — Runner/migration preparation first. No archive/consumer validation or upload until run-d-11.group-sanity status=closed and its callable manifest-check handoff is available, owner ratification recorded and both external rules (sc-lint#931 no-panic and transaction-body analyzer) delivered and passing on all changed storage code. Missing either rule blocks publication; no implicit waiver. Then final0.3.0 manifest/lock conversion, exact8-archive rehearsal with package-caps passing before upload, and fresh registry proof invoking the same check at the registry consumers. The d-12 dev bead is blocked by d-11 sanity; immediately before first upload, check the publication predicate again.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/upstream-subject — Exact close predicate: upstream beads-cache PR open with CI green at recorded SHA using published0.3.0 SDKs, URL/SHA in owned consumer README. Maintainer=user/randlee; merge not required. No response or CI failure leaves sprint open with explicit external follow-up. No local path/patch/Git SDK substitute. sc-command package exports/docs match closed d-10; cargo tree checks selected native graph, not lockfile.
All changed public storage functions are typed Result/no-panic. Actual writer-panic callers receive typed errors; required no-panic/transaction analyzer evidence is not replaced by promises or a superficial grep. cargo build --workspace passes against the final coordinated train at this closure.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps — Call d-11's single manifest check on exact unpacked SDK manifests and generated-template defaults: registry requirements must use >= tested floors with no upper bound (ANC-037). A violation fails rehearsal, registry consumer proof and upload. Consumer-owned pins are permitted and outside this default-policy check. d-12 owns input assembly/wiring; the checker stays d-11-owned and root rusqlite stays d-6-owned.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/package-caps-check — Through the same release entrypoint, controlled SDK-default fixtures with an upper bound or exact pin fail and an open-floor fixture passes. Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/registry/phase-d -p "test_manifest_gate.py". Actual archives and the registry consumer proof must also pass the check. This remains the ADR-RUN-0005 interim rule pending equivalent sc-lint#936 release and adoption.
req:REQ-RUN-0002/preserved-cron — In the actual upstream migration, the default app and cron data use the same SQLite file; the existing consumer tests verify rejection of a second active schedule with the same name and of a new schedule row at the embedding app's configured limit. Reuse the delivered cron behavior and existing upstream cases; do not build a second policy implementation (ANC-021/030/031).
req:REQ-RUN-0002/admitted-requirements — Every registry requirement this sprint writes uses >= its tested floor with no upper bound: SDK sibling/consumer >=0.3.0, rmcp >=3.9, win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0; other requirements follow the same open-floor rule. Inspect unpacked manifests and execute normal consumer tests without rewriting SDK requirements or republishing. The release-test lock and --version0.3.0/archive hashes identify the tested release, not restrictive manifest pins. Consumers may choose their own pins (ANC-037).
req:REQ-RUN-0002/release-recommendations — Release-generated applications ship the tested latest-allowed registry Cargo.lock and .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json from the same actual profile build/test run (ANC-038). Metadata enumerates every locked package name/version/source and release/toolchain/profile identity, matches Cargo.lock, and is readable for later revert/upgrade tooling. Consumers can keep, replace or update the recommended lock and pin their own requirements. Use d-11 generation code unchanged; d-12 refreshes only recommendation inputs and release proof.

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:

Selected B, coordinated8public crates0.3.0 at release; development baseline0.2.0 until d-12 conversion. Generic storage backends contain no consumer-specific table code. New atomic transaction futures are prototype risk, not copied working code.

dependencies.design:
## Approved design and authority
User direction01M76WCWNFNN7TCQ5WJ7CGQP4X supersedes withdrawn optional cron backend feature. No backend->sc-cron dependency or consumer-specific schema/SQL. sc-storage is std-only/no sc-*; public backends implement generic Storage<T> and atomic default per engine. sc-cron owns domain policy and maps CronRow through generic metadata; template schema owns WidgetRow/key/CRUD extension. Eight released packages: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite and existing sc-config/sc-transport/sc-command/sc-runtime/sc-cron/sc-cron-commands, coordinated0.3.0.
ANC-033: atomic transaction producer creates a fresh owned Send+'static future per attempt. Spec has only name and mode (read-only/read-write). Observability wrapper records name/queue wait/run time/row operations/outcome. SQLite submits one message/savepoint; Postgres/MySQL begin/commit and engine serialization retry. Read-only may use reader pool. SQLite awaits must be tx-handle operations; transaction-safe callees checked by external analyzer; actual Pending rolls back with typed error. Exact handle/row/multi-type shape is d-5 prototype decision; multi-type transactions unbuilt, not forbidden. Existing atm-core carries typed operations, not these futures: no claim this mechanism was copied/prototyped. ANC-034 forbids consumer table code in backends. ANC-035 public storage functions changed here return typed Results and never panic; ANC-036 writer panic fails all pending callers, no hang.

## Authoritative SQLite writer constraints
ANC-021..028 and ADR-RUN-0011: app/cron share default app DB/handle; one async channel, writer thread owns the only write connection; queued writes commit together and success replies follow commit. No caller blocking/spawn_blocking bridge, no SQLx SQLite driver. Only writer-owned runtime may Runtime::block_on; no Handle/futures variant exception. Reader blocking_recv needs no runtime. Domain guarantees (active-name/row-limit/per-row FENCED/atomic multi-row) are implemented once in sc-cron and tested through shared conformance. Migration is sc-cron/application code, not backend-specific CronRow SQL.

## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.

## Manifest ownership and closure builds
Every concurrently runnable pair has disjoint full-file fences. Only declared staged handoffs across a must_follow path share files: d-3 command manifest to d-10, d-5 additive contract/manifest/legacyAPI edits to d-6/7/8/9, then d-12 final shared version changes after source owners. Root Cargo adds sc-storage and one rusqlite >=0.41 requirement with no upper bound in d-5; current legacy cron and writer inherit it. D-5 absorbs legacy SQLite API drift and runs existing tests. Root Cargo.toml follows the declared d-5 -> d-6 -> d-12 handoff: d-6 owns rusqlite range qualification and d-12 changes only sc-* release versions; d-9 removes legacy DB dependency after generic conformance, not after a sibling's unobservable event. No parallel same-file edits. Single canonical root Cargo.lock owner=d-12, regenerated before exact release archives after all public source owners close. Earlier sprints build/test with regenerated temporary worktree locks; each cargo build --workspace passes at its own closure. D-12 owns0.2.0->0.3.0 and sibling literal->workspace inheritance, e.g. sc-runtime command/transport at21/22/39, sc-cron command at29/55, sc-cron-commands command/cron at19/20/27 in current source. No incompatible0.2.x public removal is uploaded.

## Requirement criterion ownership
REQ-RUN-0002/source-ranges and source compatibility = d-3; REQ-RUN-0002/published-consumers, archive/release and upstream-subject = d-12. REQ-CRON-0004/generated-app DB behavior = d-11; released beads-cache subject = d-12, relying on its actual upstream tests without duplicating generated-app criteria. Boundary sprints only implementation conformance, no feature closure. REQ-RUN-0326 no-DB+cron rejection = d-11, not Postgres/MySQL layer requirements. d-4 independent tooling integration owns CLI floor/archive/executable/report end-to-end feature, not storage integration. d-3 independent dependency feature integration owns actual crate APIs/features/CI; both integration closures have explicit vertical rationale despite first-wave location.

## Ratification and external gates
D-5 proposed template create/delete-with-generated-id extension over atomic storage preserves current DTO behavior; PENDING USER RATIFICATION. D-5 closes ADR0020 Open1-4 with dated text; pending owner ratification gates d-5 closure; layers consume its closed, frozen contract. Item5 synchronization stays deferred; ADR0021 transform and extra-path amendments record actual decision, no invented permission design. No publication before ratification. External no-panic rule randlee/sc-lint#931 and second await/transaction-safe analyzer rule (not yet requested; lead owns external request) are real dependencies, not fabricated sprint implementations. Runtime Pending detection is additional, never a substitute for build-time analysis. Mark missing external rules/approvals as blockers, never waive them in a green claim.

## Release order and gating
D-12 has a hard d-11 prerequisite in the phase index and live dev-to-sanity blockers; its branch targets the completed d-11 branch. It starts after that sanity and callable handoff. Before first crates.io upload, also require that checker passing on the exact archives, current owner ratification and actual required external rules. D-12 then final0.3.0 manifest/lock conversion, exact archive rehearsal, publish actual dependency DAG sc-storage first, and fresh registry-only proofs. All8 packages match source API/README; failure/yank/retry policy stays explicit in d-12. Upstream closure=beads-cache PR open with CI green at recorded SHA against published0.3.0; merge not required, maintainer=user/randlee. No response leaves d-12 open, no source/fork substitute. Final gate checks both integration outcomes; the d-11 prerequisite creates the explicit fourth sprint wave.

## Dependency security/qualification facts
The owner-directed workspace rusqlite requirement is >=0.41 without an upper bound, so consumers can select later security fixes. The normal test suite checks the selected versions. Rusqlite0.41 selects patchedlibsqlite3-sys>=0.39. Current SQLx umbrella features used by PostgreSQL/MySQL introduce SQLite resolution and conflict even with SQLite feature off. Direct sqlx-core/driver/macros resolve+check (lead probe), while real query!/offline/sqlx-cli remain unverified until d-7/8. Layer mixed probes compile actual driver + generic writer; d-11 qualifies complete generated mixed layouts after siblings. Always inspect selected cargo tree -i libsqlite3-sys / -i sqlx-sqlite; Cargo.lock lists optional SQLx SQLite even when not selected and is not identity proof. No downgrade to vulnerable rusqlite. All published/template registry requirements have open tested floors (ANC-037).

## Stack rule
metadata.layer is planned presentation order; sole stack writer assigns actual append-only link order by completion. pr_target is nearest consumed artifact lower bound, actual base it or descendant. No false serialization on parallel sibling's ordinal. Branch/worktree slug agrees. No implementation dispatched before plan gates.

## Lead-validated evidence (history, not delivered proof)
# run-lead validated facts (2026-11-11, plan/phase-d @ a6cc949; crates.io + rustsec advisory-db main)
1. crates.io: rusqlite 0.42.0 (published 2026-11-11T06:47Z) -> libsqlite3-sys ^0.40.0; rusqlite 0.41.0 -> ^0.39.0; libsqlite3-sys max 0.40.0. sqlx/sqlx-sqlite max 0.9.0; sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0 -> libsqlite3-sys >=0.30.1,<0.38.0. rmcp max 3.9.0.
2. RUSTSEC-2026-0459 (libsqlite3-sys, CVE-2026-119375, local WAL uninit-memory read): patched >=0.39.0; affects bundled builds 0.6.0-0.38.2. RUSTSEC-2026-0462 (rmcp, DoS): patched >=3.9.0.
3. Published sc crates at 0.2.0: sc-command, sc-config, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands, sc-runtime, sc-transport (six). sc-runtime-db-sqlite is `publish = false` -> option B must add it as a 7th published crate (or move the writer into a published crate).
4. Current pins: sc-cron rusqlite "0.39" bundled+hooks; sc-runtime-db-sqlite rusqlite "0.39" bundled; sc-command/sc-runtime rmcp "~3.8".
5. Template: store-sqlite uses sqlx 0.9 features [runtime-tokio, sqlite, macros, migrate, sqlx-toml] => bundled libsqlite3-sys <0.38 => EVERY generated SQLite app is exposed to RUSTSEC-2026-0459, with or without cron, and cannot be fixed while store-sqlite stays on sqlx 0.9. Cron opens SqliteScheduleStore at a separate path (template/config/cron.schema.json:13, crates/daemon/src/composition.rs:90, cron.rs:190).
Consequence for option A: Phase D 0.2.1 fixes the advisory for sc-cron/writer consumers (beads-cache) but generated SQLite template apps keep the vulnerable SQLite. Plan text must say so plainly; do not claim the advisory closed for generated apps.
